sections.h2: What does the housing picture look like in University Place?
sections.html:
University Place homeowners report a median home value of $624,800 in the Census Bureau's 2020-2024 estimates, and 57.2 percent of households own their home. An estimated 35,479 people lived in the city on July 1, 2025, up 1.7 percent from the April 2020 base.

The city's households earn a median of $99,031, and 19.5 percent of residents are 65 or older. Workers average 28 minutes to reach their jobs, and 87.8 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier. About 42.1 percent of adults 25 and older hold a bachelor's degree or higher, and 19.0 percent of residents speak a language other than English at home.

sections.h2: Where is University Place, and how did the city take shape?
sections.html:
University Place is a mostly suburban city in Pierce County on the west side of Tacoma, with waterfront on Puget Sound. It covers 8.34 square miles of land, sits at about 417 feet of elevation, and is bordered by Puget Sound to the west, Lakewood to the south, and Tacoma to the north and east, with Fircrest along part of the eastern edge.

The name goes back to the 1800s, when the University of Puget Sound bought land along Grandview Drive for a campus. The school ended up selling the land back for about $11,000. The area stayed unincorporated until the City of University Place was formed on August 31, 1995.

Chambers Bay is the best-known landmark. The links-style golf course opened in 2007 and hosted the 2010 U.S. Amateur and the 2015 U.S. Open. The 28-acre University Place Town Center, built in the late 2000s and early 2010s, holds the city hall, a Pierce County Library branch, the police offices, a public plaza and a mix of homes and shops. The Village at Chambers Bay has metered parking on Market Place, and the city runs parking enforcement patrols there. Cirque Park hosts community events and youth sports programs run with the Pearl Street YMCA, and the city invited residents to a Veterans Day celebration at Veterans Plaza in the park. University Place uses a council-manager form of government, with a seven-member council led by Mayor Stan Flemming.

sections.h2: Which public schools serve homes in University Place?
sections.html:
The University Place School District serves most of the city and runs eight public schools. Primary schools teach kindergarten through fourth grade, intermediate schools cover grades five through seven, junior high is grades eight and nine, and high school is grades ten through twelve.

  • Primary: Chambers, Evergreen, Sunset and University Place.
  • Intermediate: Drum and Narrows View.
  • Junior high and high school: Curtis Junior High and Curtis Senior High.

Parts of the city lie in Tacoma Public Schools and in the Steilacoom Historical School District, so check the school district on the county's parcel record before you tell a buyer which schools apply. Charles Wright Academy is also in the city.

sections.h2: What permit rules and city projects should a University Place seller watch?
sections.html:
The city requires a permit any time you construct, enlarge, alter, repair, move or demolish a building, or change its occupancy, and also for installing or replacing electrical, gas, mechanical or plumbing systems. Planning and Development Services handles them, and applications go to Permits@Cityofup.com.

Before listing, ask the department whether any finished work, such as a converted garage, a new furnace or a water heater swap, is missing a final inspection, and keep the paper trail for the buyer.

City construction can also affect access and showings near your street. The city's news page notes:

  • Work along 67th Avenue West from 40th Street West to Regents Boulevard West, adding sidewalks, landscaping and lighting, was set to begin on October 26.
  • Repair and resurfacing of Cirque Drive West from 67th Avenue West to Orchard Street was scheduled to begin September 14.
  • Grandview Senior Living is under construction at Grandview Drive West and 27th Street West.

The city also reminds residents that raked leaves belong in yard waste bags, not in the street, where they can clog storm drains and gutters.

sections.h2: What does real estate excise tax cost on a University Place sale?
sections.html:
The city's own tax page says its share of the real estate excise tax is 0.5 percent of the price, collected with the state's portion by the Pierce County Treasurer. The county keeps 1 percent of what it collects for collection costs and sends the other 99 percent to the city each month, where it may be used to finance capital projects. The state's portion is graduated, at 1.1 percent on the first $525,000 and 1.28 percent up to $1,525,000, and the Department of Revenue raises those thresholds to $551,000 and $1,551,000 for sales from January 1, 2027.

The seller owes the tax at the time of sale. The city says interest is charged if it is not paid within 30 days, and the Department of Revenue lists 6 percent as the 2026 interest rate on late excise tax. The city's tax and fee pages also cover business and occupation tax, utility tax and the fee schedule, which matter if you rent the house out or run a business from it. A sale at the $624,800 median value crosses the first state bracket, so the combined cost is a blend of rates rather than one flat figure. Ask a title company for the exact calculation.

For property tax details, call the Pierce County Assessor-Treasurer at (253) 798-6111 for assessed values, statements and senior or disability exemptions, or the treasury line at (253) 798-8678. Starting in January 2027, more Pierce County homeowners who are 61 or older, or who have a qualifying disability, will see their property taxes reduced under an expanded state program.

Washington's seller disclosure law, RCW 64.06.020, gives the buyer three business days after delivery of the form to rescind the agreement unless both sides agree otherwise. If the seller does not hand over a completed form, the buyer may waive that right before or after signing the contract.

sections.h2: Should a University Place homeowner list the house or take a cash offer?
sections.html:
Listing makes sense when the house is in good shape and you can wait for showings and a buyer's financing. A cash offer fits better when the house needs repairs, belongs to an estate, or has to close on a set date.

Compare any University Place offer on what you walk away with, not on the headline number:

  • Subtract commission, repairs, staging and carrying costs from a listing price.
  • Ask each cash buyer who pays excise tax, title and recording costs.
  • Confirm the closing date and who handles escrow.
  • Get the offer in writing, with its expiration date.

If you inherited the house, ask a probate attorney or the Pierce County Superior Court what authority you need before anyone can sign a deed.

faqs.q: How many people live in University Place?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 35,479 residents as of July 1, 2025, up from 34,866 at the April 2020 census.

faqs.q: What is the real estate excise tax in University Place?
faqs.a: The city's share is 0.5 percent of the sale price, added to the state's graduated portion, which starts at 1.1 percent on the first $525,000. The Pierce County Treasurer collects it, and the seller owes it at the time of sale.

faqs.q: Who do I call about property taxes on a University Place house?
faqs.a: Call the Pierce County Assessor-Treasurer at (253) 798-6111 for assessed values, statements and exemptions. The treasury line is (253) 798-8678.

faqs.q: Which school district serves University Place?
faqs.a: The University Place School District serves most of the city, with eight public schools including Curtis Senior High. Parts of the city fall in Tacoma Public Schools or the Steilacoom Historical School District.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to sell or fix up a house in University Place?
faqs.a: City rules require a permit to alter or repair a building or to replace plumbing, electrical, gas or mechanical systems. Email Permits@Cityofup.com to ask about records for work already done.
